title: Array of Doubled Pairs
summary: Determine if an integer array of even length can be reordered so that each element at an odd index is exactly twice the element at the corresponding even index.
statement: Determine if an integer array of even length can be reordered so that each element at an odd index is exactly twice the element at the corresponding even index.
constraints: Reorder the even-length array into pairs [x,2x].
Negative values and zero are allowed.
reference_solution:
def can_reorder_doubled(arr):
 from collections import Counter
 counts=Counter(arr)
 for x in sorted(counts,key=abs):
  if counts[x]>counts[2*x]:return False
  counts[2*x]-=counts[x]
 return True

hints: Values must be processed by absolute value so a number is matched before a farther-from-zero double.
Count values, then consume counts[x] copies from counts[2x].
Reject when the double count is insufficient.
Absolute ordering prevents a value from being consumed as a double before its own pairing demand is handled.
